To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) diaheliotropic leaf movements are more pronounced in soybean leaves grown under water stress or low nitrogen conditions; 2) diaheliotropically oriented leaves have higher rates of photosynthesis at midday compared with leaves restrained in the horizontal position, and 3) diaheliotropical leaf movements are accompanied by higher Fv/Fm ratios in leaves of well-watered and well-nourished soybean plants, but not in plants under water stress or nitrogen deficiency

diaheliotropically orienting leaves of soybean plants grown under low water availability and nitrogen deficiency had a greater reduction in Fv/Fms than leaves of plants grown with ample water and nitrogen, and that this reduction was greater in horizontally restrained leaves.

1) the magnitude of leaf movements, photosynthesis, and chlorophyll fluorescence of soybean leaves were altered by nitrogen and water availability, 2) the degree of leaf orientation was correlated with photosynthetic rates, 3) the degree of horizontal restraint was correlated with Fv/Fm, and 4) nitrogen deficiency and water stress increased the difference between orienting and restrained leaves in both photosynthesis and Fv/Fm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between leaf movement, photosynthesis, and chlorophyll fluorescence in plants grown under different nitrogen or water availabilities.
the role of diurnal heliotropism in optimizing photosynthesis and minimizing photoinhibition in plants grown under conditions of nitrogen deficiency and water stress.
the relationship between leaf movement, photosynthetic carbon assimilation, and chlorophyll fluorescence of soybean grown under contrasting nitrogen and water availability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
water and nitrogen deficiency reduced the capacity of photosynthesis, but that this reduction was less in orienting than in horizontal leaves.
the diurnal leaf movement of soybean is an adaptation to maximize carbon return on nitrogen invested in photosynthesis, and is a function of the availability of nitrogen and water.
the leaf movement response is a complex phenomenon, which is affected by many environmental factors, including light, water, temperature, and nitrogen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diaheliotropic leaf movements are associated with enhanced photosynthetic carbon gain, and are more important in environments with low nitrogen and water availability.
water stress and nitrogen availability interact to alter the diurnal patterns of leaf movement, photosynthesis and chlorophyll fluorescence in soybean.
water and nitrogen availability affect the magnitude and timing of diurnal leaf movement, photosynthesis and chlorophyll fluorescence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diurnal leaf movement is an important mechanism for plants to optimize carbon gain in a changing environment, particularly when water and nutrients are limiting.
diaheliotropic and paraheliotropic leaf movements can be used to enhance the carbon gain of soybean plants grown under water stress and nitrogen deficient conditions.

diaheliotropically orienting soybean leaves have a higher photosynthetic capacity than horizontally restrained leaves, and that this advantage is enhanced in low-nitrogen and water stressed environments.
